text:
maria: thinking out loud — we need a clearer contract for ingress teardown vs quarantine when upstream goes soft. current heuristic (connection error -> immediate teardown) is causing noisy upstream retries and duplicate work.

alex: +1. seen this with model hosts that return ephemeral 503s during GC. clients hedge and we end up double-running expensive inferences.

jamie: what's quarantine here? keep the request context but stop sending to upstream until a window passes?

maria: yeah. quarantine = hold the request in a short, bounded queue (not client socket) while we probe upstream health and maybe fallback to cheaper model variant or cached prefix. not an infinite stall — ~1s or so.

ash: sounds risky for long-poll/streaming requests. how do we handle partially-generated responses?

maria: good point. quarantine only for synchronous non-streaming requests or for streaming requests before the first token is emitted. once we start streaming, we can't easily buffer without violating latency SLOs.

ryan: proposal: introduce a "safepoint" header on ingress: `X-RW-Safepoint: <uuid|phase>` so proxies and gateways can mark whether a request is pre-output. if safepoint=pre-output, it's eligible for quarantine/hedge-window.

alex: can we make the header implicit? clients forget it. maybe infer from content-type + route config?

maria: we should default to inference routes being pre-output unless explicit `stream=true` in route config. still want the header for explicit overrides and observability.

jamie: what about billing/side-effects? if quarantine causes a later retry that triggers a charged compute run, customers will be confused. need explicit signal: `X-RW-Idempotency` + `X-RW-Quarantine-Policy` values (drop|hedge|fallback).

ash: +1 on idempotency header. also record a quarantine lifecycle event in trace so cost attribution can be mapped: `quarantine.start`, `quarantine.probe`, `quarantine.commit`/`abort`.

ops-bot: incident note: last week 3% of model invocations experienced double-charge due to quick teardown+hedge. correlating with bursts in GC.

ryan: operationally, quarantine should be local to the frontdoor instance (don't ship requests to another AZ). otherwise we lose warm KV cache affinity. local probe to upstream: probe endpoint with `HEAD /health?probe=quarantine` with backoff 50-200ms, total window configurable per route (default 750ms).

alex: need safety: cap number of quarantined requests per instance and per-tenant. otherwise latent queue becomes a DOS surface. queue-size and queue-time metrics per-tenant.

maria: agreed. defaults: max 20 quarantined reqs/instance, 200/tenant, max hold 1s. policy can be tightened for critical tenants.

jamie: implementational note: for pre-output requests we can also try quick fallback: route to smaller quantized model in 120ms if probe fails, then hedged full model if still needed. reduces waste.

ash: fallback strategy needs regulated correctness: some prompts rely on large model context. fallback must be opt-in per route.

ryan: suggestion: make quarantine a composed policy object: `{ eligibility, window_ms, local_capacity, fallback_route_id, idempotency_required }` — stored in route config.

maria: yes. also add telemetry labels: `quarantine_hit`, `quarantine_commit_type=fallback|primary`, `quarantine_duration_ms`. these will feed Optimize suggestions.

alex: one more: streaming half-open case — client disconnects while request is quarantined. we should drop it immediately, not count as a backend run. mark as `client_canceled_preoutput`.

jamie: can we add a small grammar to the contract doc? e.g., `pre-output` vs `post-output` vs `streaming` and state transitions. will write a follow-up RFC section.

maria: thanks. I'll sketch RFC patch: quarantine semantics, header wire format, default parameters, and observability requirements. cc @ryan for probe implementation and @alex for cost accounting.

ryan: ack, will prototype the probe and local queue with metrics.

alex: I'll mock cost attribution events and a billing-safeflow that prevents double-charge on aborts.

ops-bot: reminder: file follow-up RFC in `architecture/ingress-quarantine-rfc` and tag `#architecture` when ready. :memo:

maria: done for now — adding notes to RFC tracker. thanks everyone.
